vocabulary.meaning_en: a way of preparing food with heat
vocabulary.example: Steaming is a healthy cooking method.
vocabulary.note_en: method = a way of doing something

vocabulary.meaning_en: to cook something in very hot water
vocabulary.example: Boil the eggs for ten minutes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to cook something in hot oil
vocabulary.example: She fried the fish in olive oil.
vocabulary.note_en: "Fries" = long thin pieces of fried potato.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to cook food over or under direct heat
vocabulary.example: We grilled chicken in the garden.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to cook meat or vegetables in an oven or over a fire
vocabulary.note_ar: مع الأشياء الصلبة أصلاً: لحم، دجاج، بطاطس
vocabulary.example: My mother roasts a chicken every Friday.
vocabulary.note_en: Used with food that is already solid: meat, chicken, potatoes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to cook bread or cakes in an oven
vocabulary.note_ar: مع العجين والسوائل التي يعطيها الفرن شكلها
vocabulary.example: I baked a chocolate cake for her birthday.
vocabulary.note_en: Used with dough and liquids that get their shape in the oven.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to cook food using the hot gas from boiling water
vocabulary.example: Steam the vegetables for five minutes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to move a spoon around in a liquid or food
vocabulary.example: Stir the sugar into your tea.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to cut something into small pieces
vocabulary.example: Chop the onions finely.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to cut something into thin flat pieces; a thin flat piece
vocabulary.note_ar: a slice of pizza = شريحة بيتزا
vocabulary.example: Slice the tomatoes for the sandwich.
vocabulary.note_en: a slice of pizza = one thin flat piece of pizza

vocabulary.meaning_en: to put things together and combine them
vocabulary.example: Mix the flour and the eggs in a bowl.

vocabulary.meaning_en: instructions for cooking a dish
vocabulary.example: Can you give me the recipe for this soup?

vocabulary.meaning_en: one of the foods you use to make a dish
vocabulary.note_ar: من اللاتينية: الأشياء التي «تدخل» في الطبخة
vocabulary.example: You only need three ingredients for this cake.
vocabulary.note_en: From Latin: the things that "go into" a dish.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a thing you hold in your hand to do a job
vocabulary.example: A good knife is the most important kitchen tool.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a flat metal container for frying food
vocabulary.example: Heat some oil in a pan.
vocabulary.note_en: frying pan = a flat pan for frying

vocabulary.meaning_en: a deep round container for cooking
vocabulary.example: The soup is in the big pot.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a box-shaped machine that cooks food inside with heat
vocabulary.example: Put the bread in the oven for 20 minutes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the top part of a cooker where you put pots and pans
vocabulary.example: Don't leave the stove on.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a tool with a sharp blade for cutting
vocabulary.example: Be careful with that knife.
vocabulary.note_en: The k is silent. Plural: knives.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a flat board you cut food on
vocabulary.example: Put the carrots on the cutting board.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a deep round dish for mixing or eating
vocabulary.example: Break the eggs into a bowl.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a kitchen tool for beating eggs or cream; to beat quickly
vocabulary.example: Whisk the eggs until they are light.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the special taste of food
vocabulary.example: This ice cream comes in ten flavors.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something added to what is usual
vocabulary.example: Cheese costs one dollar extra.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a white substance that makes food taste salty
vocabulary.example: Add a little salt to the water.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a hot spice, usually black or white
vocabulary.example: Pass me the salt and pepper, please.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a thick liquid used in cooking
vocabulary.example: Don't use too much oil.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a sweet white or brown substance
vocabulary.example: I take my coffee without sugar.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a powder or seed that gives food a strong taste
vocabulary.note_ar: spice نوع واحد، و spices أنواع كثيرة معاً
vocabulary.example: Cumin is my favorite spice.
vocabulary.note_en: "Spice" is one kind; "spices" are many kinds together.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a thick liquid served with food
vocabulary.example: Would you like tomato sauce with your fries?

vocabulary.meaning_en: the flavor of food; to try a little food
vocabulary.example: Taste the soup before you add salt.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having a very good taste
vocabulary.example: This pasta is delicious!

vocabulary.meaning_en: to tell someone about a possible danger
vocabulary.example: The teacher warned us about the test.

vocabulary.meaning_en: giving attention to avoid danger or mistakes
vocabulary.example: Careful! The pan is hot.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make something hot
vocabulary.example: Heat the milk but don't boil it.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the gray gas that comes from something burning
vocabulary.example: The kitchen was full of smoke.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a sudden loud burst, like a bomb
vocabulary.example: We heard a loud explosion.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to succeed in doing something difficult
vocabulary.example: I finally managed to open the jar.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in a way that is not clear or known
vocabulary.example: Somehow, we arrived on time.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to not go near someone or something
vocabulary.example: Stay away from the edge of the cliff.

fine_lines.title: chop vs slice
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان بمعنى «يقطّع» لكن الشكل مختلف. chop يعني تقطيع الشيء إلى قطع صغيرة مثل المكعبات (البصل، الجزر). slice يعني تقطيعه إلى شرائح رقيقة مسطّحة، و slice نفسها تعني «شريحة».

examples.sentence: Chop the onions into small pieces.
Slice the tomatoes for the burger.
Can I have another slice of pizza?

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean to cut, but the shape is different. "Chop" means to cut something into small pieces like cubes (onions, carrots). "Slice" means to cut it into thin, flat pieces; a "slice" is one of those pieces.

fine_lines.title: bake vs roast
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان طهي في الفرن، والسرّ في القوام. bake للأشياء التي تدخل الفرن عجيناً أو سائلاً ليس لها شكل صلب، والفرن هو الذي يعطيها شكلها (خبز، كيك، بسكويت). roast للأشياء الصلبة أصلاً التي ندخلها الفرن لتنضج وتتحمّر (لحم، دجاج، بطاطس، خضار). لا نقول roast a cake ولا bake a chicken.

examples.sentence: I baked a cake this morning.
We roasted a chicken with potatoes.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean cooking in the oven; the secret is the texture. "Bake" is for things that go in as dough or liquid with no solid shape, and the oven gives them their shape (bread, cake, cookies). "Roast" is for things that are already solid, which we put in the oven to cook and turn brown (meat, chicken, potatoes, vegetables). We don't say "roast a cake" or "bake a chicken".

fine_lines.title: at the end vs in the end
fine_lines.explanation_ar: at the end تعني «في نهاية شيء محدد» ويأتي بعدها غالباً of: at the end of the movie / street / month. أما in the end فتعني «في نهاية المطاف / أخيراً» بعد أحداث كثيرة، ولا يأتي بعدها of.

examples.sentence: The shop is at the end of the street.
We tried many restaurants, but in the end we ate at home.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "At the end" means at the end of a specific thing, and is usually followed by "of": at the end of the movie / street / month. "In the end" means finally, after many things happened, and is not followed by "of".

fine_lines.title: has gone to vs has been to
fine_lines.explanation_ar: has gone to تعني أنه ذهب وما زال هناك ولم يرجع بعد. has been to تعني أنه ذهب إلى المكان من قبل ورجع، فهو ليس هناك الآن.

examples.sentence: Ali isn't here. He has gone to the supermarket.
I have been to that restaurant many times.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "Has gone to" means he went there and is still there; he hasn't come back yet. "Has been to" means he went there before and came back, so he is not there now.

fine_lines.title: filled with vs full of
fine_lines.explanation_ar: لا فرق حقيقي بينهما في المعنى. was filled with مبني للمجهول، و full of صفة، ويمكنك استخدام أيٍّ منهما: The room was filled with smoke / The room was full of smoke.

examples.sentence: Her eyes were full of tears.

fine_lines.explanation_en: There is no real difference in meaning. "Was filled with" is a passive form and "full of" is an adjective, and you can use either: The room was filled with smoke / The room was full of smoke.

expressions.phrase: out of the frying pan, into the fire
expressions.meaning_ar: خرج من مشكلة ليقع في مشكلة أسوأ (كالمستجير من الرمضاء بالنار)
expressions.example: He left his stressful job for one with lower pay and longer hours: out of the frying pan, into the fire.
expressions.meaning_en: to escape one problem and fall into a worse one

expressions.example: It's either a barbecue or an explosion!
expressions.meaning_en: only two choices: one thing or the other

expressions.example: I always follow the recipe carefully.
expressions.meaning_en: to do the steps of a recipe as written

expressions.example: They managed to cook a delicious dish.
expressions.meaning_en: to succeed in doing something difficult

expressions.example: You should stay away from the knives!
expressions.meaning_en: to keep a distance from something; to avoid it

grammar.title: Ellipsis: leaving out repeated words
grammar.explanation_ar: الإسقاط (ellipsis) هو حذف كلمات مفهومة من السياق لتجنّب التكرار. 1) نحذف الفعل المكرّر في الجزء الثاني من الجملة. 2) نحذف كل ما بعد الفعل المساعد، وهذا شائع جداً في المقارنات. 3) في الكلام اليومي غير الرسمي نحذف الفاعل (وأحياناً الفعل المساعد) من بداية الجملة.
examples: I'll handle the design, and you (will handle) the marketing.
I ate an apple, and Maya (ate) a pear.
She has read the book, but I haven't (read the book).
(Do you) Want some tea? / (I) Don't know.
grammar.explanation_en: Ellipsis means leaving out words that are clear from the context, to avoid repeating them. 1) We leave out a repeated verb in the second part of the sentence. 2) We leave out everything after the helping verb; this is very common in comparisons. 3) In informal everyday speech we drop the subject (and sometimes the helping verb) at the start of a sentence.

grammar.title: Present perfect: been to vs gone to
grammar.explanation_ar: مع المضارع التام: have/has gone to = ذهب وما زال هناك. have/has been to = سبق له أن ذهب ثم عاد. إذا كان الشخص أمامك الآن فلا تقل He has gone to London.
examples: Ahmed has gone to London. (He is there now.)
Ahmed has been to London. (He went and came back.)
Where's Ali? He has gone to the shop.
grammar.explanation_en: With the present perfect: have/has gone to = went there and is still there. have/has been to = went there before and came back. If the person is standing in front of you now, don't say "He has gone to London."

grammar.title: One article for joined nouns
grammar.explanation_ar: عندما نعطف اسمين مرتبطين معاً يكفي أن نذكر أداة التعريف the مرة واحدة: the pan and cutting board، the knife and fork.
grammar.explanation_en: When we join two related nouns, we only need to say "the" once: the pan and cutting board, the knife and fork.

questions.question: To cut onions into very small pieces is to ___ them.
questions.explanation_ar: chop = يقطّع قطعاً صغيرة، و slice = شرائح.
questions.explanation_en: To chop = to cut into small pieces; to slice = to cut into thin pieces.

questions.question: Which is correct?
choices: I chopped a cake in the oven.
questions.explanation_ar: الكيك يدخل الفرن عجيناً، فنستخدم bake.
questions.explanation_en: A cake goes into the oven as a batter, so we use "bake".

questions.question: We ___ a chicken with potatoes in the oven.
questions.explanation_ar: الدجاج له قوام صلب أصلاً، فنستخدم roast.
questions.explanation_en: A chicken is already solid, so we use "roast".

questions.question: Ali isn't home. He ___ to the supermarket.
questions.explanation_ar: ذهب وما زال هناك: has gone to.
questions.explanation_en: He went and he is still there: has gone to.

questions.question: I know that café. I ___ there many times.
questions.explanation_ar: سبق أن ذهبت ورجعت: have been.
questions.explanation_en: I went there before and came back: have been.

questions.question: We tried many plans, but ___ we stayed at home.
questions.explanation_ar: in the end = في نهاية المطاف، بدون of.
questions.explanation_en: "In the end" = finally, after everything; no "of" after it.

questions.question: "Out of the frying pan, into the fire" means:
choices: going from a bad situation to a worse one
questions.explanation_ar: الخروج من موقف سيئ إلى موقف أسوأ.
questions.explanation_en: Going from a bad situation into a worse one.

questions.question: Which tool do you use to beat eggs?
questions.explanation_en: A whisk is a kitchen tool for beating eggs.

questions.question: "She has read the book, but I haven't." What is left out after "haven't"?
questions.explanation_ar: حذفنا كل ما بعد الفعل المساعد: haven't (read the book).
questions.explanation_en: We left out everything after the helping verb: haven't (read the book).

questions.question: A list of steps and ingredients for cooking a dish is a:
questions.explanation_en: A recipe = the instructions for cooking a dish.
